content.rendered:
San Francisco is home to many night markets, popping up in various neighborhoods throughout the city. One of the city’s popular night markets is returning this Friday, September 25, with an array of local vendors, free activities, and live performances.

Sunset Night Market September 25

This Friday, the Sunset Night Market will take over 5 blocks in the Sunset with rows of local vendors and live entertainment. The popular night market will run from 5 to 10 pm on Irving Street and is open to all ages. This month’s market will celebrate the Autumn Moon Festival with mooncakes, lanterns, and plenty of fun activities and performances.

title.rendered: 30 minutes from SF: California’s ‘Italian Riviera’ is hosting a 3-day marine festival this weekend with luxury yachts and harbor views

content.rendered:
Sausalito, often called California’s “Italian Riviera” for its Mediterranean harbor atmosphere, provides the backdrop for one of the Bay Area’s most anticipated marine events this weekend.

The Sausalito Boat Show returns to Clipper Yacht Harbor from Friday, September 25 through Sunday, September 27, 2026, with sailboats, powerboats, luxury yachts, electric vessels, charter yachts, and a packed program of activities for all ages.

content.rendered:
Sundown Cinema is one of San Francisco’s most popular free events, bringing movie screenings to parks across the city. The program took a brief hiatus last summer but returned in full for 2026, and the next free movie screening is in less than a week.

Sundown Cinema September 2026

The next Sundown Cinema is Friday, September 25, at the Ferry Building. The family-friendly comedy classic School of Rock is the featured film of the night, and you can enjoy pre-screening activities. The movie will start after sunset, but we recommend getting there early to scope out a good spot. After the September screening, there will be only one more Sundown Cinema in 2026, featuring the classic Halloween movie Beetlejuice at Crane Cove Park.

content.rendered:
San Francisco has no shortage of historic bars, but this one comes with a rather unexpected backstory. The Treasure Island venue occupies The Administration Building, the former Pan Am Airport Terminal, a striking 1930s building that once welcomed passengers heading across the Pacific by flying boat. Yes, you read that right. Flying boat.

Today, the space has been transformed into an Art Deco-inspired whiskey tasting room, but traces of its glamorous aviation past remain. And if the building looks vaguely familiar, there’s a good reason: it has also had a starring role in a major Hollywood blockbuster.

You could once fly to Asia from here

Pan Am’s famous China Clipper flying boats operated from Treasure Island from the late 1930s into the mid-1940s. Instead of taking off from a runway, the enormous aircraft landed and departed directly from the water in Clipper Cove.
